conversation.content: Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling now that your baby has arrived. We’ll use a short, well-studied questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**—usually just called the **EPDS**. It’s simply 10 questions about your mood and well-being over the past seven days. Your answers stay between you and your care team; there’s no right or wrong, and we go at your pace. When you’re ready, I’ll ask the first question.
Hi Sarah, thank you. I’m ready whenever you are.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah, I still laugh—maybe not as much as before the baby, but when my husband makes silly faces while changing diapers, I definitely chuckle. I’d say most of the time I can see the funny side.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
I do find myself looking forward to little things—like taking the baby for a walk in the stroller or having coffee with my neighbor. Not every moment, but pretty often. I’d say most of the time.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong
Not really. If the baby spits up a lot or won’t settle, I might think “Did I eat something weird?” for a second, but I don’t stay stuck on it. I’d say I blame myself only occasionally.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll suddenly wonder if the baby’s breathing okay when he’s napping, even though I can see him on the monitor. It’s not constant, and it usually passes once I peek in the crib, but it does pop up now and then.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
No, I haven’t had that kind of scared or panicky feeling.
Things have been getting on top of me
Now and then, like when the baby won’t nap and the laundry’s piling up, I feel a little swamped, but mostly I catch up and feel okay. I’d say only occasionally.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
No, my sleep’s been fine. Once the baby settles for the night, I can usually fall back asleep pretty easily.
I have felt sad or miserable
I’ve had a couple of moments where I felt a little blue—usually when I’m really tired—but it doesn’t last long. I wouldn’t say I’ve been truly sad or miserable.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
No, I haven’t cried from feeling unhappy. Maybe once I teared up when I was overtired, but that’s it.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, that hasn’t crossed my mind at all.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 6: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum adult (partner present)

Primary endorsed symptoms  
- Mild, transient worry about infant safety (no impairment)  
- Occasional feeling “swamped” when tasks accumulate; resolves with support  
- Brief tired-related low mood, no persistent sadness, crying, or anhedonia  

Patterns  
- Preserved capacity for enjoyment and humor  
- No excessive guilt, self-blame, or hopelessness  
- Sleep disruption solely infant-driven; returns easily once infant settled  
- No panic episodes, no self-harm ideation  

Screening significance  
- Sub-threshold for major depressive or anxiety disorder; findings most consistent with normative postpartum adjustment  
- No current safety concerns (denies self-harm, suicidal, or infanticidal thoughts)  

Risk factors absent  
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, guilt, sleep–mood linkage, panic, or self-harm thoughts  

Observation  
Postpartum mood screening negative for depression or clinically significant anxiety at this time. Continue routine support and re-evaluate if symptoms intensify or persist beyond two weeks.
